label: Bible Study
prompt: For all have _____, and come short of the glory of God;
verse: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
note: The great leveler — 'all' is why the Romans Road starts here.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: The LORD is my light and my _____; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
verse: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
note: Two rhetorical questions with only one honest answer: nobody, and no one.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a _____ for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
verse: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
note: Abraham's answer on Moriah: God will provide himself a lamb — a promise bigger than he knew.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For the earth shall be filled with the _____ of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
verse: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
note: Habakkuk's anchor amid Babylonian dread: God's glory will one day be as unavoidable as the ocean.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very _____, and of tender mercy.
verse: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
note: 'Very pitiful' meant full of pity — the word drifted over the centuries; the tender mercy didn't.
